newsitem.title: UK: BT shrugs off Kirch venture talk report.
newsitem.headline: BT shrugs off Kirch venture talk report.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Tuesday declined to comment on a newspaper report that the company was in talks with the Kirch group to launch interactive services using digital satellite television in Germany.
"We talk to a lot of people," stated a spokesman for the company. "This is pure speculation. We can't comment."

The Financial Times newspaper reported that BT and Kirch were involved in "detailed negotiations" that also included a joint venture with DF1, a digital satellite company that launched 19 channels of digital television in November.

As telecoms companies suffer stiffer competition in domestic markets and are forced to defend their traditional market, BT has said that it will be actively pursuing opportunities in Germany, Italy, Spain and the Netherlands in the near future.
BT plans to become the second operator in each European country by winning a share five to 10 percent share of the market over the next five to seven years.
With full liberalisation of the European telephone markets earmarked for 1998, telecoms companies are expanding abroad to bolster earnings.
